note: Proof (process_rest linear loop). The branch `if(key%d){cnt_dead++; return;}` is taken only if d>1, d=gcd(g,m), g=gcd(lg1,lg2), m=lmod. The only linear component in any level (24, 48, 96 have nlin=0,0,1) is p=75118313082913 with m=29406683 prime, lg1=28249472, lg2=23976715 (both nonzero mod m, identical for every multiset because the lift lattice and prime list depend only on the level; unit/lin_probe.py prints them for 3 multisets). d divides the prime m, so d=m iff m divides g, which divides lg1; lg1<m and lg1>0, so d=1 and key%1==0: the mutated branch is unreachable.

name: m_lvlN_L4_redc_no_sub
find: static inline ull redc(u128 T, ull p, ull ninv){ ull m=(ull)T*ninv; ull t=(ull)((T+(u128)m*p)>>64); return t>=p?t-p:t; }
replace: static inline ull redc(u128 T, ull p, ull ninv){ ull m=(ull)T*ninv; ull t=(ull)((T+(u128)m*p)>>64); return t; }
note: Proof (lvlN.c redc/powmod_mont/powmod_mont_n). p odd, p<2^54. Intermediate REDC outputs are only ever multiplied again; for inputs r,x<2p, t<(4p^2+2^64 p)/2^64<2p, so the lazy value stays <2p, no u128 overflow, and is congruent mod p. Only the final redc(r) is observed (used as the subgroup-table key in factor_log). There T=r<2p, m<=2^64-1, so t>=p needs r+m*p>=p*2^64, i.e. m=2^64-1 and r>=p, i.e. r=p (r<2p<2^64 and m=r*ninv forces r=p mod 2^64). r=p means y^e=0 mod p, impossible for y in [1,p-1] (zero y is counted as cnt_zero before any exponentiation). So the output is identical with and without the subtraction. Evidence: unit/test_redc_equiv.c reaches pre-subtraction values >=p in 20932 of 1.09e9 redc calls over all 15 level primes and finds 0 differing outputs in 3e7 powmods.
